q: What goes wrong if I build the music first and fit the voice in later?
a: The voice ends up squeezed in and fighting the music. Set dialogue first: type the clips and Auto-Match them (`essentialSound.autoMatch`) or run Clean Up Voice (`audio.cleanupVoice`), then bring music and effects up underneath.

q: Can I run noise reduction on the music track as well?
a: Better not: noise reduction belongs on the dialogue. On music or effects it only adds artefacts; keep Voice Isolation for changing noise and Reduce Noise for steady hiss on the voice clips.

q: How strong should the DeEss be?
a: DeEss 3–6 in Essential Sound is the usual range. It works after EQ and compression, which bring sibilance up; too much and the speaker lisps.

q: How long should a dialogue crossfade be?
a: A few frames. Long crossfades on dialogue make words overlap; the point is only to stop the click at the cut.

q: Why pan effects but leave voices centred?
a: Phones and many TVs fold to mono or are heard off-axis; centred voices survive that. Pan effects and ambience with Essential Sound ▸ Pan or the Panner, leave dialogue pan at 0.
